THE SINGULAR MEAN BOUNDARY OF ORIGINAL J_r
31 October 2026. Solo structural theorem for actual periodic gradients.

1. THE ALL-FIELD CLASSIFICATION

Fix ANY r>0 and retain the original homogeneous quartic J_r. For every
real mean-zero actual periodic G=Dphi in L4 set

 H_G=<J_r''(G)> in Sym_4, v_G=<DJ_r(G)>, f_G=<J_r(G)>.

Theorem. If G is nonzero, H_G has rank either THREE or FOUR. It is
singular if and only if

                 G(x)=u tensor e_j h(x_j), j=1 or 2,     (1)

where u is a fixed nonzero real output vector and h is a nonzero
mean-zero one-variable L4 profile. The coordinate line must support
periodic frequencies on the given torus; on the square torus (1) is
literal. There is no bandwidth, amplitude or concentration restriction.

For every such singular field, the minimum over ALL affine means is
finite and attained. If R=u tensor e_j and m_k=<h^k>, then

 inf_M [<J_r(M+G)>-J_r(M)]
       =J_r(R)[m4-(2/3)m3^2/m2] >=f_G/3>0.               (2)

Every minimizing mean is

             M=-(m3/(3m2))R+K, K in ker H_G.             (3)

In particular an arbitrarily large component of the mean along this
kernel cannot reveal a hidden negative energy.

Consequences. Covariance rank at least TWO already makes H_G positive
definite. Full four-dimensional covariance is unnecessary for ordinary
mean elimination. For EVERY actual field, including the singular ones,

 inf_M Delta_Jr(M,G)=f_G-v_G^T H_G^+ v_G/2               (4)

is attained; v_G belongs to range H_G. Any strict actual QC failure of
the original J_r must have H_G positive definite. These statements do
not assert a uniform modulus or continuity when fields approach the
singular set; the fourth-order angular contact is not erased.

2. EXACT ACOUSTIC KERNELS AND OPPOSITE DETERMINANT SIGNS

Put t_r=(2r+1)/3 and U_u=[[u1,-u2],[u2,u1]]. The independent all-r ROC
proof in ../quartic_coupling/original_roc.py gives positive definite
J_r''(u tensor xi) whenever xi is off the two coordinate axes.
On the axes its rank is exactly three, with kernels

 ker J_r''(u tensor e1)=span{U_u K1}, K1=[[0,t_r],[1,0]],
 ker J_r''(u tensor e2)=span{U_u K2}, K2=I.               (5)

The receiving code rebuilds the actual polynomial, all kernel equations
in r,u1,u2, and the positive complementary blocks. The transported null
matrices satisfy

              det(U_u K1)=-t_r |u|^2<0,
              det(U_u K2)=|u|^2>0.

ZERO-WEIGHT NORMAL RELAXATION: AN ACTUAL a^(-2/3) LIMIT
31 October 2026. Solo construction, full normal-infimum theorem and exact field.

1. WHAT THE ZERO-WEIGHT BOUNDARY CHANGES

The earlier attained normal coefficient at scale 1/a assumes the fixed
actual Hessian field S is bounded away from zero. Dropping that condition
is not a harmless use of a pseudoinverse. There are actual compatible
fields for which the coefficient infimum at scale 1/a is MINUS INFINITY.
The full normal relaxation has a different, sharp scale a^(-2/3).

This note proves a weak-L4 Gamma limit and convergence of the ENTIRE
normal-fiber infimum, including arbitrary a-dependent normal correctors.
Its limiting nonlinear cost is attained. The Hessian Hodge fiber remains
fixed: arbitrary simultaneous variation of that fiber is not asserted.

An explicit piecewise-polynomial example uses the original N901 coupling
at r=3/4 and its already admitted globally QC quartic completion. Its
actual normal-curl support is disjoint from the base Hessian support,
yet the Poisson/Hodge extension has a nonzero interaction with the base.
The receipt verifies a strict finite-a energy lowering and a POSITIVE
total Jensen gap. This is a structural relaxation theorem and obstruction
to a tempting approximation, not a Morrey counterexample.

2. SETUP AND EXACT RESCALED EXPANSION

Let F0 be any real homogeneous quartic on R^(2x2), H its restriction to
Sym(2), and delta>0. For A write z(A)=A12-A21 and define

 F_a(A)=F0(A)+2delta a z(A)^2 |sym A|^2+delta a^2 z(A)^4.  (1)

For the N901 application this is exactly the coupling-preserving family
proved globally ROC and QC in ../quartic_coupling/PROOF.txt, with all
coefficients of the original off-Sym coupling retained. The limit below
is algebraic/variational and does not assume a QC implication for F0.

Fix a bounded actual Hessian field S=M+D^2 psi, M symmetric, on a
normalized flat torus. Put w=|S|^2 and Z=L4_0, the real mean-zero scalar
L4 space. For z in Z set

 E_z=-J Hess Delta^(-1)z, Y_z=sym E_z, J=[[0,-1],[1,0]].   (2)

This is an ACTUAL mean-zero vector gradient with curl z, and its
Hessian Hodge component is zero. It parameterizes the entire normal
fiber at this fixed Hessian component. The retained elementary Hodge
bounds give ||E_z||_2=||z||_2, ||Y_z||_2<=||z||_2 and
||E_z||_4<=32||z||_4.

Let K=Delta^(-1) div div[J DF0(S)], with its zero mode removed.

Informed prior-exposed coordinator assessment,not blind.

The singular classification is a real all-field theorem for the ORIGINAL J_r, for every r>0. The averaged acoustic Hessian has rank three or four for nonzero actual periodic gradients. Singularity forces a one-variable rank-one profile on one acoustic axis, with one common output direction. The proof uses exact kernels and opposite determinant signs on the two axes, followed by a positive Fourier/Parseval decomposition. It is not a covariance law presumed realizable. On that face the affine-mean minimum is attained, equals `J_r(R)[m4-(2/3)m3^2/m2]` and is at least one third of the positive quartic moment. The constant is sharp over profiles. Kernel components of the mean cannot uncover an unbounded negative direction.

An important distinction: covariance rank is not the rank of the affine-mean Hessian. Covariance rank at least two already makes the latter positive definite. The pseudoinverse formula for mean elimination now holds for every actual field, including the singular ones. This removes an unnecessary search assumption. It does NOT give a uniform bound while approaching the singular set with concentrations or divergent means. The fourth-order acoustic contact and earlier independent capacity discontinuity remain.

Additional compatibility reductions control covariance rank at most two for the stated ROC quartics, and rank-three fields with a rank-one annihilator. The remaining rank-three class has the exact representation `T Hess psi`, with invertible T reduced by actual output symmetry/scale to two continuous shape parameters and an orientation sign. The scalar potential remains unrestricted and infinite dimensional. This is not a reduction of every full-covariance field to that class, nor a finite-dimensional solution of Morrey's problem. The author explicitly credits the elementary reductions as classical, without a priority claim.

The normal-relaxation result genuinely repairs the prior infimum/limit gap. For any fixed bounded Hessian field S, every normal corrector in L4 is included, even if it depends on a. At the 1/a scale the complete infimum has the extended-real weighted dual coefficient `-(1/(8 delta)) min_ell integral (K-ell)^2/|S|^2`, with the correct zero-weight convention.
